application_type: Legacy SOAP Web Service (JAX-WS, Java 6, JBoss AS 5.1)

findings.title: SOAP RPC/Encoded Interface Not Agent-Consumable
findings.description: The service exposes a single SOAP 1.1 endpoint using deprecated RPC/encoded style. Modern AI agent frameworks cannot natively consume RPC/encoded SOAP. No REST or OpenAPI interface exists.
findings.remediation: Expose functionality as a REST/JSON API with an OpenAPI 3.x specification.

findings.title: Hand-Maintained WSDL Drifts from Implementation
findings.description: The WSDL is manually maintained and acknowledged to drift from the implementation. An agent relying on the WSDL contract cannot trust it reflects actual service behavior.
findings.remediation: Auto-generate the interface contract from code, or migrate to OpenAPI with contract testing.

findings.title: No Programmatic Authentication Implemented
findings.description: No authentication logic exists in the source code. The service accepts all requests without verifying caller identity.
findings.remediation: Implement OAuth 2.0 client credentials or API keys with per-agent identity and scoped permissions.

findings.title: Hardcoded Database Credentials in Source Code
findings.description: Database connection credentials are hardcoded as string constants in the Java source, exposed in version control.
findings.remediation: Move credentials to a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) and inject at runtime.

findings.title: No Idempotency or Duplicate Detection
findings.description: The submitOrder operation performs a direct SQL INSERT with no duplicate detection. Re-submitting the same order creates duplicate records.
findings.remediation: Implement idempotency keys with server-side dedup or enforce a unique constraint on (partner_id, po_number).

findings.title: No Approval Workflow or Rate Limiting
findings.description: The service immediately executes the database insert on any submitOrder call with no approval step, spending limit, rate limiting, or circuit breaker.
findings.remediation: Implement order amount thresholds requiring human approval, rate limiting per partner/agent, and a review queue.

findings.title: No Logging, Monitoring, or Tracing
findings.description: The service has zero observability instrumentation. No logging framework, no metrics, no distributed tracing, no health check endpoint.
findings.remediation: Add structured logging with correlation IDs, health endpoints, request metrics, and distributed tracing.

findings.title: Plaintext Credentials Over Unencrypted HTTP
findings.description: The service endpoint uses plain HTTP (no TLS). Any authentication tokens transmitted would be interceptable.
findings.remediation: Enforce TLS (HTTPS) for all service communication.

findings.title: No Transaction Management
findings.description: No explicit transaction boundaries, commit, or rollback logic. Connection is opened and closed per request without error handling.
findings.remediation: Use proper transaction management with commit/rollback and connection pooling.

findings.title: No Input Validation
findings.description: No validation of partnerId, poNumber, or amount values. Any string is accepted and written to the database.
findings.remediation: Add type checking, range validation, and business rule enforcement at the service boundary.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Errors are returned as unstructured strings. No SOAP faults, error codes, or machine-parseable error structures.
findings.remediation: Define structured error response schemas with error codes agents can programmatically handle.

findings.title: Exception Messages Leaked to Callers
findings.description: Raw Java exception messages including internal details are returned to the caller.
findings.remediation: Return generic error messages to callers; log details server-side.

findings.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
findings.description: XML parsing uses default DocumentBuilderFactory settings with no XXE protections. An agent passing XML with external entity references could trigger SSRF, read local files, or cause denial of service.
findings.remediation: Disable external entities and DTD processing in DocumentBuilderFactory.

findings.title: SQL Injection
findings.description: User-supplied values from parsed XML are directly concatenated into SQL statements. An agent or attacker can execute arbitrary SQL against the database.

security_vulnerabilities.title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
security_vulnerabilities.description: XML parsing uses default DocumentBuilderFactory settings with no XXE protections.
security_vulnerabilities.impact: Server-side request forgery, local file read, denial of service.

security_vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
security_vulnerabilities.description: User-supplied values from parsed XML are directly concatenated into SQL statements.
security_vulnerabilities.impact: Arbitrary SQL execution, data exfiltration, modification, or deletion.

remediation_priorities: Critical Security Fixes (XXE, SQL injection, hardcoded credentials, TLS)
Idempotency and State Safety (idempotency keys, transaction management)
